text:
The philosophical butterfly

settles on the pink star

and thus forms a window of hell

The masked man is always standing before the naked woman

whose hair slips just as, in the morning, the light of a lamp

that they forgot to extinguish

The wise furniture prepares the room that performs sleight of hand

with its rosettes

its circular rays of sunlight

its glass grindings

inside which a sky blues with precision

in memory of the inimitable breast

Now the cloud of a garden passes over the head of the man

who has just sat down

It splits in half the woman with the magical bust and Parma eyes

It is the hour when the boreal bear, with an expression of great intelligence

stretches and accounts for a day

On the other side, rain rears over the boulevards of a great city

Rain through the fog with rivulets of sunlight over red flowers

Rain and the diabolo of olden times

Legs beneath the fruit-bearing cloud surround the greenhouse

Only the pulse of a very white hand is perceived, represented

by two tiny wings

The seesaw of absence swings between the four walls

Splitting heads

From which flocks of kings escape and immediately wage war

Until the eastern eclipse

Turquoise at the bottom of the cups

reveals the equilateral bed of sheets the color of those flowers called

snowballs

The delightful bedside tables, the torn curtains

within reach of a little book bearing these words stamped on it

There is no tomorrow

whose author bears a strange name

in the dark terrestrial signage

translation.title: Hotel of Sparks
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the dream logic of the masked man, magical woman, eastern eclipse, and “There is no tomorrow.”
